correctness.rationale: The source's system (2.2) resets B=(h1,yB) to ((1+p1)h1,yB−tau1); the successor map must therefore use f(A)=yB−tau1−yA. Theorem 3.1 instead prints yB(1−p1)−yA. In the strict case the model gives f(A)>0. The printed argument asks for f(A1)<0, chooses an impact height yB1>yB, and prints f(A1)=yB1−yB>0 before applying the intermediate value theorem. The same-sign printed values do not imply a zero. Even the corrected f(A1)=yB1−tau1−yA1 has no negative sign established by yB1>yB alone. In the equality case the admissible first return closes at A. This is a diagnosis of the printed argument, not a counterexample to the theorem or to its numerical example. The supplied checker was inspected as an algebraic witness only; the conclusion follows directly from the source reset and proof.
